newsitem.title: USA: Aon expects cost savings in second half.
newsitem.headline: Aon expects cost savings in second half.

text.p: Aon Corp chief executive Patrick Ryan said the company has targeted cost savings opportunities from the consolidation of its recent acquisitions but does not expect to begin to seem them until the second half of the year.
"The primary benefit from our cost savings efforts will begin to be realized in the second half of 1997, with the full annualized operating impact achieved in 1998," Ryan said.
However, the company's first quarter results were hurt by the additional operating and financing costs associated with those acquisitions, he said in a statement.
The company reported first quarter operating earnings before special charges of $0.51 a share compared with $0.56 a share a year ago.
The First Call consensus estimate was $0.69 a share.
Special charges of $145 million pretax, or $0.54 per share after-tax, were recorded in the first quarter, mostly in connection with the acquisition of with Alexander & Alexander.
Aon also last year acquired British broker Bain Hogg.
The company reported a first-quarter net loss per share of $0.02 compared with a profit of $0.69 a year ago.
"We are pleased with the current status of our consolidation process and are on schedule to merge our businesses worldwide," Ryan said.
"At this stage, we have identified the framework for our merged organization and targeted the cost savings opportunities," he added.
Growth in Aon's insurance brokerage and consulting businesses stemmed mostly from the additions of Alexander & Alexander and Bain Hogg, Ryan said.
Aon's insurance brokerage and consulting businesses reported first quarter 1997 revenue growth of 82 percent to $881 million from $485 million last year.
"Aon Group's overall results continue to reflect the competitive industry environment," Ryan said.
The performance of the insurance and other services segments was helped by internal growth, he said, especially the international retail businesses.
But the reinsurance brokerage business, he said, continued to suffer from difficult market conditions throughout the industry.
The insurance underwriting operations showed good results for the quarter, enhanced by strong revenue and earnings growth from the extended warranty business, he said.
Aon's insurance underwriting businesses posted revenue growth of two percent in the first quarter 1997 to $445 million.
Pretax operating income increased 11 percent to $65 million.
